title: Revelation 12:7–17
context: War breaks out in heaven, and Michael and his angels throw down the dragon, the ancient serpent called the devil and Satan. Heaven celebrates that the accuser is cast down, and the saints overcome him by the blood of the Lamb and their testimony. Enraged, the dragon pursues the woman, who is protected, and then makes war on the rest of her offspring, who keep God’s commandments and hold the testimony of Jesus.

verses.text: There was war in the sky. Michael and his angels made war on the dragon. The dragon and his angels made war.
verses.arminianNotes: Michael and his angels fight the dragon. Some date the war to a primeval fall of Satan, others to Christ’s victory at the cross, and some to a future event.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers commonly connect the war with Christ’s victory at the cross and ascension, as verses 10–11 suggest.

verses.text: They didn’t prevail. No place was found for them any more in heaven.
verses.arminianNotes: The dragon loses his place in heaven.

verses.text: The great dragon was thrown down, the old serpent, he who is called the devil and Satan, the deceiver of the whole world. He was thrown down to the earth, and his angels were thrown down with him.
verses.arminianNotes: The dragon is named: the old serpent, the devil, Satan, deceiver of the whole world. Arminian readers see deception as his chief weapon.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers see the serpent of Genesis 3 defeated, in fulfillment of Genesis 3:15.

verses.text: I heard a loud voice in heaven, saying, “Now the salvation, the power, and the Kingdom of our God, and the authority of his Christ has come; for the accuser of our brothers has been thrown down, who accuses them before our God day and night.
verses.arminianNotes: The accuser of the brothers is thrown down. Arminian readers see that Christ’s victory silences Satan’s charges against believers.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers see the accuser silenced because Christ’s death has answered every charge (Romans 8:33–34).

verses.text: They overcame him because of the Lamb’s blood, and because of the word of their testimony. They didn’t love their life, even to death.
verses.arminianNotes: They overcame by the blood of the Lamb and the word of their testimony and did not love their lives to the death. Arminian readers see Christ’s victory received and lived out by faithful believers.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers see the Lamb’s blood as the ground of victory and faithful testimony as its fruit.
verses.keyContrast: Both agree the victory rests on the Lamb’s blood. Arminian readers stress the believers’ faithful testimony as their participation in it. Reformed readers stress that the testimony itself is the fruit of Christ’s finished work in them.

verses.text: Therefore rejoice, heavens, and you who dwell in them. Woe to the earth and to the sea, because the devil has gone down to you, having great wrath, knowing that he has but a short time.”
verses.arminianNotes: Heaven rejoices, but woe to the earth, because the devil knows his time is short.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers see Satan’s fury as the rage of a defeated enemy.

verses.text: When the dragon saw that he was thrown down to the earth, he persecuted the woman who gave birth to the male child.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers see the church as the target of Satan’s hostility.

verses.text: Two wings of the great eagle were given to the woman, that she might fly into the wilderness to her place, so that she might be nourished for a time, times, and half a time, from the face of the serpent.
verses.arminianNotes: She is given eagle’s wings, recalling the exodus (Exodus 19:4), and is nourished for a time, times, and half a time.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers see God’s care for his church in the world.

verses.text: The serpent spewed water out of his mouth after the woman like a river, that he might cause her to be carried away by the stream.
verses.arminianNotes: The serpent spews a flood after her.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers see attempts to overwhelm the church by persecution or deception.

verses.text: The earth helped the woman, and the earth opened its mouth and swallowed up the river which the dragon spewed out of his mouth.
verses.arminianNotes: The earth helps her and swallows the flood.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers see God using his creation to protect his people.

verses.text: The dragon grew angry with the woman, and went away to make war with the rest of her offspring, who keep God’s commandments and hold Jesus’ testimony.
verses.arminianNotes: The dragon makes war on the rest of her offspring, who keep God’s commandments and the testimony of Jesus. Arminian readers see faithful believers who obey and witness.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers see believers in every generation as the target of Satan’s war, marked by obedience and testimony.
